ledger.sentence: Dopamine antagonist anti-sickness medicines are used to treat nausea and vomiting, and metoclopramide is the member covered on this site.
ledger.note: NHS metoclopramide page; class named in assignment

ledger.sentence: The MHRA has restricted metoclopramide to short-term use because of the risk of serious neurological side effects.
Metoclopramide is grouped with domperidone in NHS formularies, and the sources used here do not describe the group's mechanism in more detail.
The MHRA says the risk of acute neurological effects is higher in children than in adults, and that in children aged 1 to 18 it is only a second-line option.
Epilepsy and Parkinson's disease are listed by the NHS as conditions where metoclopramide may not suit someone.
The NHS asks people taking Parkinson's disease medicines, drowsiness-causing medicines or other anti-sickness medicines to speak to a doctor or pharmacist first.
The NHS says uncontrollable movements such as tics, tremors, muscle stiffness and spasms are the most common serious side effect of metoclopramide.
